claims.object_text: epilepsy (generalized seizures) reported in 71% of probands and 36% of relatives
claims.quote: (a) epilepsy, mainly presenting with generalized seizures, reported in 71% of probands and 36% of siblings or first/second-degree relatives.

claims.object_text: intellectual disability reported in 100% of probands and 13% of relatives
claims.quote: (b) ID reported in 100% and in 13% of probands and siblings or first/second-degree relatives, respectively;
(c) learning disabilities detected in 28% of the SLC6A1 carriers, all of them were relatives of a proband;
(d) around 51% of the whole cohort presented with psychiatric symptoms or behavioral disorders, including 82% of the probands.

claims.object_text: ASD diagnosed in 40% of those with psychiatric symptoms
claims.quote: Out of the 19 patients with psychiatric symptoms, ASD were diagnosed in 40% of them;

claims.object_text: neurological findings (primarily tremor and speech difficulties) observed in 38.5% of cohort
claims.quote: (e) neurological findings (primarily tremor and speech difficulties) were observed 38.5% of the whole cohort, including 10 probands.
Our families harbored 12 different SLC6A1 variants, one was a frameshift, two stop-gain, while the remaining were missense.

claims.object_text: mild intellectual and/or learning disabilities in first- or second-degree relatives (less severe phenotype)
claims.quote: first-or second-degree relatives presented with a less severe phenotype, featuring mainly mild intellectual and/or learning disabilities, at variance with the probands who suffered from moderate to severe ID, generalized, sometimes intractable, epileptic seizures, behavioral and psychiatric disorders.
